title: Activepieces vs Flowise: Features & Pricing (2026)
summary: Activepieces vs Flowise identifies which tool fits your needs: Flowise for building AI agents, Activepieces for automating business apps with audit trails.
body_markdown:
## What Flowise does well, costs, and lacks


Flowise is strong at building LLM applications, agents and retrieval pipelines on a visual canvas, and thin at coordinating business processes across everyday apps.


By connecting nodes for models, vector stores and memory, you assemble chains, agents and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG, where a model answers from your own documents) in Flowise.


The output is a chatbot or agent you can test and embed. If the thing you ship is the LLM app itself, that's the job it was designed for.


### Flowise pricing, hosting and licence


You can self-host Flowise, which is open source under Apache 2.0, and it also sells a managed cloud.


Cloud tiers are metered in predictions, meaning each call to your flow. The Free tier allows[100 predictions a month](https://comparedge.com/tools/flowise/pricing) , according to CompareEdge, which covers a prototype but not a public chatbot.


At 400 messages a day, a bot would exhaust Starter's 10,000 in about 25 days. Pro allows 50,000, five times Starter, which suits a modest production assistant but means a busy customer-facing bot needs headroom planning.


### Flowise admin controls and integrations


Check which tier a security review would require before you commit, because SSO and role-based access may not be included in every plan. Its integrations are mostly LLM-side: model providers, vector databases, document loaders and tools.


Consider a six-step flow. Step 4 strips HTML from a fetched page, step 5 asks GPT-6.1 Sol to score the site from 0 to 100 and write a 120-word summary, and step 6 creates a Google Docs document.


The model call is one step in six; the rest is fetching, cleaning and filing.


That ratio is the limit for non-LLM work. Flowise handles step 5 well, and the surrounding app-to-app steps are where you would be writing your own nodes or glue code.


If the deliverable is the agent itself, evaluate Flowise first: a RAG assistant over internal documents, or a chat widget with custom retrieval logic. Its LLM-specific nodes give finer control over that than a general automation tool does.


### Where the LLM builder is the right call


Judged on the job, Flowise wins whenever the deliverable is the model-facing app.


Its nodes for chains, memory, vector stores and agent tool use are the product rather than an add-on, so a developer tuning retrieval works closer to the problem than in a general automation tool.


On hosting and licence it is easy to defend. Apache 2.0 means a team can read, fork and run the code with no commercial agreement, and a small team can start on the free self-hosted build or the free cloud tier without a sales conversation.


For a prototype or a single-purpose assistant, that is a lighter start than a platform built for company-wide processes.


Governance and reach are where it gives ground, as the sections above show. But a few developers shipping one assistant, with no reviewer asking for SCIM or git-synced environments, may never need what Activepieces adds. For them the narrower tool is the better one.
